# Samples

**All files here are SYNTHETIC.** They were generated by `tests/fixture_factory.py` and `tests/benchmark_lib.py`
(no real company, person or account data). "Scanned" PDFs were made by rasterising a generated digital PDF and
embedding the pictures into a new PDF with no text layer (optionally adding skew/noise/blur) — they are *simulated* scans.

| File | Document type | What it exercises |
|---|---|---|
| `invoice_ruled.pdf` | digital, ruled | 12 columns, 40 rows over 2 pages, repeated header, title, page footer |
| `inventory_ruled.pdf` | digital, ruled | 10 columns, 55 rows, SKU leading zeros (`00001`), blank cells |
| `bank_ruled.pdf` | digital, ruled | header only on page 1 (header-less continuation), blank debit/credit cells, 60 rows |
| `wide_16col.pdf` | digital, ruled | 16 columns at 6.5 pt |
| `invoice_unruled.pdf` | digital, no lines | 12 columns found from word geometry |
| `bank_unruled.pdf` | digital, no lines | centred title above the table, repeated header |
| `sparse_unruled.pdf` | digital, no lines | ~25 % blank cells |
| `wrapped_ruled.pdf` | digital, ruled | multi-line cell text (works) |
| `wrapped_unruled.pdf` | digital, no lines | multi-line cell text — **documented weak spot** (extra rows, flagged) |
| `purchase_order.pdf` | digital, 2 tables | line items with a **Total** row + delivery schedule on a new page |
| `invoice_scanned.pdf` | simulated scan | no text layer → OCR, 40 rows over 2 pages |
| `bank_scanned_skewed.pdf` | simulated scan | 1° skew + noise |
| `bank_scanned_degraded.pdf` | simulated scan | 130 dpi, −1.5° skew, heavy noise/blur — expected to be **rejected** |
| `mixed_digital_scanned.pdf` | mixed | page 1 digital, page 2 scanned, one table across both |

`generated_outputs/` holds, for each PDF above, the `.xlsx` workbook and `_validation.csv` **actually produced by the
pipeline** (`python scripts/run_benchmark.py --save-samples`). They were produced by running the pipeline on these exact
files; none were hand-edited. Regenerate them any time with that command (or `python -m pytest`).

Ground truth for each file lives in `tests/benchmark_lib.py` (hand-written literals for the bank statement and purchase
order; seeded generators for the rest — expected cells are the strings printed into the PDF).
To try your own file, just upload it in the app.
